newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian PM signs gas pipeline access decree-agency.
newsitem.headline: Russian PM signs gas pipeline access decree-agency.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin has signed a decree outlining new rules on access to gas pipelines, Russian news agencies said, but a Chernomyrdin spokesman said he was unaware the decree had been signed.
Interfax said the decree, called "The Situation on the Order of Access for Independent Gas Producers to the Gas Transport System" had been signed on Monday.
Viktor Konnov, Chernomyrdin's spokesman, said he was unaware of the decree, when asked to confirm the reports.
But officials have said that imminent changes to access to the gas pipeline system were on the cards.
The decree is designed to free up access to the pipeline system for independent gas producers, Interfax news agency said, quoting First Deputy Fuel and Energy Minister Sergei Kiriyenko.

It forms part of a move by President Boris Yeltsin's dynamic reformist cabinet to introduce more competition to Russia's so-called natural monopolies, which include the gas, oil, electricity and railway industries.
It was not immediately clear how the decree would affect Russian monopoly gas producer Gazprom, the world's largest gas producer and a key exporter to Western Europe.

The company accounted for around 95 percent of Russian natural gas output in 1996. The government is trying to make way for more independent producers to compete on the domestic market, and freer access to pipelines is part of this plan.
Gazprom produced 565 billion cubic metres (bcm) of natural gas in 1996, up 5.2 bcm from 1995. It plans to boost annual output by 120-130 bcm in 12 to 15 years.
